subject: Request: regional burst credits & latency guardrail — SLA addendum
messages:
From: Rachel Lim <rachel@holohealth.io>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@holohealth.io
Date: 2028-07-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SLA ask for onboarding (regional burst / latency credits)

Hi Kimberly / Ben —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re close to contract signature but a couple of product/ops asks came up from our platform team that we need to capture in an addendum before procurement signs the MSA:

- Regional burst protection: during scheduled and unscheduled traffic spikes we need explicit burst-credit language so our tenant won’t be throttled for short high-throughput windows (we expect occasional batch imports).
- Latency guardrail: we need a definition of degraded-mode latency thresholds and an associated credit schedule if 95th percentile across our primary region exceeds 300ms for more than a rolling 1-hour window.
- Telemetry & evidence: what telemetry will Redwood provide (per-tenant latency histograms, per-request trace ids, timeline of failover events) and can you include a runbook/evidence matrix as an appendix?

Can you confirm whether this is something you can add to the SOW/order form (we are not asking to change the MSA itself, just a targeted addendum + an exhibit)? Procurement would like draft language to review.

Thanks —
Rachel
Rachel Lim
Director, Platform Engineering
HoloHealth

Hi Rachel —

Appreciate the clear asks — we can do an SLA addendum that sits alongside the MSA and the SOW. A few clarifying Qs so we prepare a single clean draft for your procurement: 

1) Regions in scope — you referenced "primary region" in the note. Can you confirm which region(s) you want covered for the burst-protection language (us-east1, us-west2, eu-west1)?
2) Burst window semantics — do you want a rolling 10-minute window for spike tolerance or a 60-minute window? We can propose both (short burst credits vs sustained surge).
3) Credit mechanics — do you prefer a token-based credit (X credits per hour) or a service-credit percent of monthly invoice for each breach band?

We’ll loop in legal for the precise redline and accounts for the billing/credit mechanics. I’m cc’ing Marissa (legal) and Ben (lead AE) so they can weigh in — we’ll target a first-draft addendum for you by EOD Friday.

If it helps, we have a standard evidence matrix (what telemetry we provide + sample charts) that we can attach as an ops exhibit.

Best,
Kimberly Park

To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-19T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: SLA addendum draft language (internal redline)

Kim / Ben —

Attached is a short-form redline for the addendum that addresses the three asks. High-level notes: 

- Regional scope: I kept the language flexible and added an appendix table to enumerate covered regions per order form (this lets field teams toggle regions without MSA changes).
- Burst credits: proposed a two-tier approach — "burst credit" (4 x 10-minute tolerance windows per calendar day) + "sustained surge" credit band for >60-minute sustained high throughput. That should cover both batch imports and longer-load events.
- Latency guardrail: defined breach as 95th percentile latency > 300ms over any rolling 1-hour window in a covered region. Credit = pro rata service-credit tiers (0.5% / 1.5% / 3% of monthly invoice by severity band).
- Evidence: added an "Ops Evidence Matrix" appendix listing telemetry we will provide (per-tenant p95/p50 histograms, request-level trace ids for sampled requests, failover timeline, and deployment roll events). I noted an SLA evidence request response time of 5 business days.

If this aligns, I’ll prepare a docx and an ops-exhibit spreadsheet for signature. I flagged two policy items for legal/ops review before sending externally: 1) retention window for per-request traces (we default to 30 days, client may ask longer), and 2) whether we expose sampled request IDs to external callers or provide them as part of the evidence package.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Hi Rachel / procurement team —

Thanks for the quick responses and the clarifications. Attached is the draft SLA Addendum (HoloHealth_SLA_Addendum_v1.docx) and the Ops Evidence Matrix (ops-evidence-matrix.xlsx). Summary of the main points included: 

- Regional burst protection: addendum lists covered regions on the order form; short bursts (10-minute windows) are tolerated up to 4 occurrences/day; sustained surges (>60 minutes) fall into a separate credit band.
- Latency guardrail: breach defined as p95 > 300ms over any rolling 1-hour window. Credit schedule: 0.5% / 1.5% / 3% of monthly invoice per severity band.
- Evidence & runbook: per-tenant latency histograms (p50/p95), sampled request trace ids (retained 30 days by default), failover/region-fail timeline, and an incident runbook excerpt. SLA evidence requests will be responded to within 5 business days.

Next steps: 
1) Please review the attached draft and confirm the regions to include (we defaulted to us-east1 and us-west2 per the earlier conversation).
2) If approved, we’ll route the doc for signature via DocuSign (link below) and coordinate with Billing to set the credit mechanics on the order form.
